sandbox_observations: The runtime is read-only with restricted networking/capabilities. Codex could not create PATH aliases due to the read-only filesystem. gcloud's snap launcher was denied cap_dac_override before any auth query. Supabase DNS/UDP socket access was denied. Vercel encountered DNS failure and timed out. tsx could report its version but could not create its /tmp IPC socket. Docker's Windows shim is visible, but Docker Desktop WSL integration is unavailable. These are sandbox/runtime denials, not authentication failures. The only credential-shaped exported process variable observed was VSCODE_GIT_IPC_AUTH_TOKEN; the other listed names came from readable ./.env.local and apps/web/.env.local files.
gaps_and_notes: Codex-side MCP configuration is empty: /home/justi/.codex/config.toml contains only the trusted project /home/justi/dev/customer-portal and a TUI model-availability section. It has no MCP server or profile sections, so this runtime has none of the Claude harness MCP configuration. With a write-capable sandbox, Codex could create/update its PATH aliases, tsx could create its local IPC socket, and tools could write ordinary caches/config state. Network and snap-capability access would still need explicit allowance to validate gcloud, Supabase, Vercel, Docker, psql connections, npm registry auth, and Twilio credentials. Per-seat handling is appropriate for GitHub tokens, gcloud user OAuth/access-token databases, Supabase access tokens, Vercel login/OIDC identity, Twilio profiles, and Codex ChatGPT sessions. Git identity in repository-local .git/config and project .env.local files are currently shared workspace state; shared secret files should be separated or tightly allowlisted if seats require distinct identities. GitHub is definitively unauthenticated because its stored token is invalid. gcloud, Supabase, Vercel, Docker, and remote psql auth remain unknown because execution/network restrictions prevented a valid auth test.
